"Currently, the company's visibility for the third quarter has improved compared to the previous month, with overall performance expected to outperform market expectations," it added, without giving details. However, Foxconn said it remained necessary to "monitor the impact of the volatile global political and economic situation". It likewise did not elaborate. Foxconn, formally called Hon Hai Precision Industry, does not provide numerical forecasts. It said revenue last month rose 51.98% from a year earlier to T$921.8 billion ($29.15 billion), the highest amount ever for August and the second month in a row it has exceeded T$900 billion. Foxconn's shares closed up 3.4% on Friday, before the revenue data was released, outperforming the broader market's (.TWII) 1.5% gain. ($1 = 31.6210 Taiwan dollars)

item.title: How escalating attacks are upending daily life in Kyiv
item.description: Commuters stranded; children rushed underground in the middle of the school day; festivals cancelled; walks punctuated by booming air defences. Near-constant drone attacks are the stark new reality in Kyiv, and daily life is likely to get harder.
item.dc:creator: Olena Harmash, Anna Voitenko
item.content:encoded: Commuters stranded; children rushed underground in the middle of the school day; festivals cancelled; walks punctuated by booming air defences. Near-constant [USN:L1N44W0FE TEXT:"drone attacks"] are the stark new reality in Kyiv, and daily life is likely to get harder. Kyiv has survived many traumas since Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022. Despite the initial shock of war and the advent of attack drones and ballistic missiles, residents adapted and managed to impose a semblance of normality. But as a fifth full winter of war approaches, that is becoming harder to maintain. Over the summer, Moscow began sending swarms of high-speed, jet-propelled drones that are more destructive and harder to shoot down than older propeller-powered models. For the last 10 days, air attacks have been around-the-clock rather than mainly at night, puncturing Ukrainians' sense that their country's own long-range drone campaign against Russia was swinging the war back in their favour. Vitaliia Poliakova and her partner were driving near a bridge on the eastern bank of the Dnipro on Thursday when a jet-powered drone struck the road near their car, injuring both. "We were driving, talking about our own things. Then there was a sudden hit," the 35-year-old said, speaking in the back of an ambulance. Poliakova had cuts to her right hand and her partner had a bloodied face and right leg. BRUTAL WINTER AWAITS Foremost in the minds of many of Kyiv's 3 million residents is the approach of winter. Russian attacks have caused regular power and water outages since early in the war, but their intensity in the last 10 days points to greater disruption. "The last year has been really difficult for us," said Bohdan, 29, as he surveyed his damaged apartment block, struck in a Russian attack earlier this week. "After this (attack), as you can see, it will probably be even harder, so we're moving away." With frontline fighting causing hundreds of casualties a week but yielding little in terms of territorial gains, Russia and Ukraine have engaged in an escalating air war in recent months, hammering each other's energy and logistics facilities. The U.N. has verified more than 16,000 civilian deaths so far in the conflict, the vast majority of them in Ukraine. Both Moscow and Kyiv say they do not target civilians, but in Kyiv and the surrounding region, dozens of civilians have been killed since August 27. COMMUTING AND SHOPPING GET HARDER AND HARDER On Monday, repeated air raid alerts halted metro services linking the two sides of the Dnipro river that divides the city. At Osokorky station near the opposite bank to the centre, nurse and psychologist Yulianna Oliynyk and her two sons waited on a packed platform for the alarm to be lifted. "I'm already thinking maybe we should just take sleeping bags and sleep in the metro at the station near the school," she said. "Last year it was difficult at school and now I honestly don't even know what to do. I just don't know." Roads into central Kyiv are clogged, bus stops are crammed and people are walking long distances to get to and from work. Grocery shopping is becoming more difficult. Large supermarkets close when air raid sirens sound, meaning customers must leave the building mid-shop. Some dairy items are running low as supply chains are disrupted and warehouses are hit. Natalia Petrivska, executive director at the Ukrainian Food Retail Alliance, appeared on television this week to reassure people that they did not need to panic buy. SCHOOLS RETURN DESPITE NEW DANGERS Russia fired more than 2,800 jet-powered drones at Ukraine in August, air force spokesperson Yuriy Ihnat said, after increasing their use fivefold in July compared with June. Interception rates were at around 60%, he added, compared with more than 90% for slower, conventional drones. Russia says such attacks have a military purpose; Ukraine says they are designed to break civilian morale and persuade the government to give up territory at a time when Washington appears to be making a [USN:L8N44V0GQ TEXT:"new push for peace"]. Yet polling by the Kyiv International Institute of Sociology in August showed attitudes towards Russia hardening. The number of respondents who opposed ceding the unoccupied part of the Donbas region - one of Russian President Vladimir Putin's key demands - rose to 69% from 62% in April. On the first day of the new academic year this week, pupils at one Kyiv school had just finished their first class when air raid sirens sounded and they hurried to underground shelters to continue their studies. "It's stressful for them, but the children are becoming better able to adapt," said headmaster Roman Feshchuk. Around 400 children were enrolled this year at the school, which was damaged in an earlier Russian attack in May, although fewer first-graders had signed up, Feshchuk told Reuters. Oleksandra, a young girl wearing a traditional Ukrainian dress and carrying flowers to celebrate the new academic year, said she particularly enjoyed arts and crafts. Asked what she dreamed of, she replied: "That the war will end."

item.title: Japan score nine tries in comfortable 57-12 win over Canada
item.description: Hooker Mamoru Harada scored two tries as Japan warmed up for the start of the Pacific Nations Cup next week with a comprehensive 57-12 victory over Canada in Niigata on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Hooker Mamoru Harada scored two tries as Japan warmed up for the start of the Pacific Nations Cup next week with a comprehensive 57-12 victory over Canada in Niigata on Saturday. Celebrating 100 years since the formation of the Japan Rugby Football Union in 1926, the home side scored nine tries in all as they dominated the forward battle and were able to find space for their electric backs. Props Takato Okabe and Takumi Inaba, flankers Ben Gunter and Kanji Shimokawa, centre Yuya Hirose, lock Harry Hockings and back row Tiennan Costley also crossed for scores, with eight of their nine tries coming from forwards. Canada, who will also take part in the Pacific Nations Cup, were outgunned up front, but managed tries through fullback Takoda McMullin and centre Ben LeSage. It was by no means perfect from Japan, who had numerous handling errors and were at times put under pressure in the scrum. But when keeping it at close quarters among the forwards, they gained regular metres and were strong in defence to limit Canadian opportunities in their own 22. Japan face the United States in their Pacific Nations Cup semi-final in Higashiosaka next Saturday, while Canada meet Fiji at the same venue in their last four clash.

item.title: MLB roundup: Guardians earn two walk-off wins in DH sweep of Tigers
item.description: Brayan Rocchio hit his second homer of the game, a solo shot in the bottom of the ninth inning, giving the Cleveland Guardians a come-from-behind 7-6 win over visiting the Detroit Tigers in the first half of a day-night doubleheader on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Brayan Rocchio hit his second homer of the game, a solo shot in the bottom of the ninth inning, giving the Cleveland Guardians a come-from-behind 7-6 win over visiting the Detroit Tigers in the first half of a day-night doubleheader on Friday. Rocchio belted a grand slam in the fourth inning off Keider Montero, then went deep against Drew Sommers (1-4) as the Guardians overcame a 6-1 deficit. Cade Smith (4-1) pitched the ninth for the win, joining Craig Yoho and Erik Sabrowski in tossing a combined four scoreless innings. Max Clark had three hits and two RBIs for the Tigers, and Spencer Torkelson homered and singled. Montero worked four innings, allowing six runs on eight hits. Guardians 4, Tigers 3 (Game 2, 10 innings) Travis Bazzana singled home Brayan Rocchio with two outs in the 10th inning, giving Cleveland its second walk-off win of the day over Detroit. Hunter Gaddis (3-3) pitched two perfect innings for the Guardians, who had lost four of six entering the day. Bazzana hit a game-tying, two-run homer in the eighth inning as Cleveland overcame a 3-0 deficit. Kevin McGonigle had two hits and an RBI for the Tigers, who fell for the 16th time in 20 games. Kenley Jansen (4-6) took the loss. Dodgers 5, Nationals 3 Blake Snell delivered six scoreless innings, Kyle Tucker contributed a home run and Los Angeles topped visiting Washington. Teoscar Hernandez had a two-run double, one game after hitting a two-run game-ending double. The Dodgers won their second consecutive game without Shohei Ohtani, who is dealing with a sore knee, biceps and neck. Snell (3-1) gave up five hits and struck out seven. James Wood had two doubles and drove in a run for the Nationals, who lost their second consecutive game after winning five of six. Brewers 10, Reds 7 Rookie Cooper Pratt ripped a bases-clearing triple and scored on a wild pitch during a five-run fifth inning, lifting Milwaukee past host Cincinnati. David Hamilton had an RBI triple and William Contreras added a run-scoring double for the Brewers, who own the majors' best record and have won seven of their last 10 games. Entering the box to his new walk-up song, Lee Greenwood's "God Bless The USA," Venezuela-born Eugenio Suarez belted a three-run homer for the Reds in his return from a two-game absence in order to take the U.S. naturalization test. Braves 5, Phillies 2 Chris Sale outdueled Cristopher Sanchez in a battle of aces and Mauricio Dubon hit a late two-run homer as visiting Atlanta topped Philadelphia in a matchup of the National League East's top two teams. Sale (14-9) allowed two runs and six hits in six innings. Sanchez (16-5) also tossed six innings, giving up three runs on five hits. Ronald Acuna Jr. had an RBI single as part of a 3-for-5 night for the Braves, who earned their ninth win in 11 games. Alec Bohm produced a solo homer and an RBI double for the Phillies, who took their second straight loss. Bryce Harper had his career-high on-base streak end at 35 games. White Sox 4, Twins 1 Colson Montgomery hit a two-run homer -- one of three Chicago long balls -- and the White Sox ended a two-game skid with a win over visiting Minnesota. Miguel Vargas and Braden Montgomery each hit solo homers for the White Sox, while Tristan Peters collected two hits. Erick Fedde (8-8) defeated the Twins for the second time in less than a week, tossing five shutout innings. Josh Bell went 2-for-3 and homered to plate Minnesota's lone run. Kody Clemens finished 3-for-4 for the Twins, who have dropped back-to-back games after winning three in a row. Pirates 1, Angels 0 Jared Jones matched his season high with nine strikeouts over six three-hit innings and Jake Mangum had an RBI double to lead Pittsburgh past visiting Los Angeles. Bryan Reynolds had two hits for the Pirates, who won for the fifth time in the past six games. Konnor Griffin, activated off the 60-day injured list after missing 49 games with a finger injury, scored the lone run of the contest in the second inning. Jones (3-6) walked one while snapping a seven-start winless drought, throwing a season-high 91 pitches, 63 for strikes. Angels starter Ryan Johnson (3-8) gave up one run on four hits in six innings. Cubs 6, Marlins 1 Shota Imanaga outdueled Janson Junk to lead Chicago past host Miami as the Cubs won their second straight game and took over the top spot in the National League wild-card standings. Imanaga (9-10) allowed one run on three hits over six-plus innings. Aaron Civale followed with three scoreless innings of one-hit ball to log his second save. Michael Busch homered, and Nico Hoerner had three hits and an RBI. Junk (6-9) tossed five innings, giving up three hits and one run. Griffin Conine had half of the Marlins' four hits and scored their lone run. Red Sox 1, Orioles 0 Ranger Suarez fired seven sharp innings and Mickey Gasper homered in the first, lifting Boston to a victory at Baltimore. Suarez (6-4) limited the Orioles to five hits and one walk while striking out three across a 91-pitch effort. Garrett Whitlock and Aroldis Chapman (32nd save) each pitched an inning in relief to complete the shutout. Shane Baz (5-15) lasted 6 1/3 innings, yielding one run on four hits as the Orioles lost their fourth in a row. Blaze Alexander registered three of Baltimore's six hits, which were all singles. Mets 10, Giants 6 Nolan McLean worked through six innings and won his third straight decision as host New York beat San Francisco. Mark Vientos hit a three-run homer in the first to give the Mets a lead they never relinquished. Francisco Alvarez went deep twice while Bo Bichette and Francisco Lindor each had two-run homers to back McLean (11-8), who allowed two runs on six hits. Rafael Devers went 3-for-4 with a two-RBI double and a three-run homer for the Giants, who have dropped three of four. Turner Hill finished 2-for-4 with a run-scoring single. Rookie Matt Wilkinson (0-3) yielded seven runs (four earned) in three innings. Astros 3, Diamondbacks 1 Yainer Diaz homered, Cristian Javier matched his season high in strikeouts and Houston defeated visiting Arizona. Javier (2-5) allowed one run on one hit with eight strikeouts in five innings as the Astros won for the seventh time in nine games. Josh Hader struck out the side in the ninth for his 23rd save, making him the 41st player in history to record 250 career saves. The Diamondbacks took their fourth loss in five games as Merrill Kelly (9-13) worked six innings, allowing three runs on seven hits. Gabriel Moreno hit a solo homer. Blue Jays 9, Royals 2 Alejandro Kirk and Ernie Clement had two hits and a pair of RBIs apiece to help visiting Toronto post a victory over Kansas City. After Blue Jays starter Jameson Taillon exited with elbow discomfort following two innings, four relievers combined to throw seven innings of one-run ball. George Springer also drove in two for the Blue Jays, who won their sixth game in seven tries. Daniel Lynch IV (4-5) allowed five runs on seven hits across five innings for the Royals, who have lost four of their last five. Bobby Witt Jr. and Vinnie Pasquantino bookended the loss with solo homers for Kansas City. Cardinals 7, Rockies 6 Ivan Herrera hit a three-run homer in the ninth inning, and St. Louis rallied to beat Colorado in Denver. The Cardinals trailed 6-4 when Thomas Saggese drew a leadoff walk from Jordan Romano (0-3) and stole second before Jose Fermin reached on a throwing error. Herrera hit a 1-2 slider 430 feet to center. Cade Winquest (1-0) earned his first major league win with 1 2/3 innings of scoreless relief, and Riley O'Brien got the final three outs for his 36th save. Cole Carrigg hit an inside-the-park home run and tripled while TJ Rumfield also went deep, tripled and singled for Colorado. Padres 3, Yankees 2 (10 innings) Luis Campusano belted a two-run homer in the bottom of the 10th inning, giving San Diego a win over visiting New York. Facing Paul Blackburn (7-3), Campusano belted a first-pitch sinker an estimated 394 feet to left field. Mason Miller (5-2) pitched two innings to earn the win despite allowing Spencer Jones' RBI single in the top of the 10th that gave New York a short-lived 2-1 edge. Max Fried threw 5 2/3 innings of one-run ball for the Yankees, who had won four of their previous five games. Ben Rice hit a solo homer among his three hits. Athletics 7, Mariners 6 Max Muncy, Alika Williams, Jeff McNeil and Zack Gelof homered in a five-run third inning and the Athletics held on for a victory at Seattle. Brady Basso (1-2) pitched three scoreless innings of relief as the A's won their third consecutive game. Hogan Harris worked the ninth for his 15th save. Cal Raleigh homered for the Mariners, who have dropped seven of the past nine. Logan Gilbert (11-9) was tagged for seven runs on eight hits over 4 2/3 innings, including all four homers, though he struck out 10. --Field Level Media

item.title: Explosions près de l'île iranienne de Kharg, dans le golfe Persique
item.description: Des explosions ont été entendues samedi près de l'île iranienne de Kharg, dans le golfe Persique, où se trouve un important terminal pétrolier, a rapporté l'agence de presse semi-officielle Fars.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Des explosions ont été entendues samedi près de l'île iranienne de Kharg, dans le golfe Persique, où se trouve un important terminal pétrolier, a rapporté l'agence de presse semi-officielle Fars. L'agence de presse officielle Nournews a indiqué avoir reçu des informations non confirmées de sources locales selon lesquelles un pétrolier iranien naviguant près de Kharg aurait ait été la cible d'un missile tiré par les forces américaines. Selon un correspondant de l'agence Fars présent sur l'île de Kharg, des bruits d'explosion ont été entendus en provenance du Golfe, mais aucune fumée n'a été aperçue. Les autorités iraniennes n'ont fait aucun commentaire dans l'immédiat sur ces informations.

item.title: Iranian tanker hit by US attack near Iran's Kharg Island, Tasnim says
item.description: An Iranian tanker was hit by U.S. forces on Saturday near Iran's key oil export hub, Kharg Island, in the Gulf, the semi-official Iranian news agency Tasnim reported.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: An Iranian tanker was hit by U.S. forces on Saturday near Iran's key oil export hub, [USN:L1N44S09M TEXT:"Kharg Island"], in the Gulf, the semi-official Iranian news agency Tasnim reported. According to a Tasnim correspondent from Kharg, the tanker was hit by four U.S. missiles in the area of Kharg Island's anchorage. Tasnim quoted local sources as saying there were no casualties and the tanker's crew was being evacuated. There was no immediate official announcement by Iranian authorities and U.S. Central Command did not immediately respond to a request for comment. U.S. President Donald Trump said on August 31 in a one-line social media post accompanied by an AI-generated video that Kharg Island was being "blown to smithereens". Iranian authorities have vowed a strong response if Kharg is attacked. Iran is the third-largest producer in the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and exported 90% of its crude via Kharg Island before the war, but flows have been disrupted since a U.S. blockade of Iranian oil exports began in mid-April. Trump said on June 11 that he wanted to take over Kharg Island, but then said a threatened U.S. military operation there was [USN:O8N40E018 TEXT:"off the table"] for now, days before Tehran and Washington signed an interim agreement aimed at ending the war on June 17. A U.S. attack on Kharg would heap further pressure on Iran's oil industry and its wider economy, which is already reeling from the U.S. naval blockade. The U.S. imposed its blockade on Iranian ports after Iran effectively shut the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway that carried one-fifth of the world's oil supply before the war.

item.title: Top 25 roundup: Malachi Toney sets receiving record for No. 7 Miami
item.description: Darian Mensah threw for 401 yards and five touchdowns in his debut as the Hurricanes' quarterback and Malachi Toney caught 12 passes for a school-record 234 yards and three touchdowns to lead No. 7 Miami to a comfortable 45-6 victory at Stanford on Friday night.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Darian Mensah threw for 401 yards and five touchdowns in his debut as the Hurricanes' quarterback and Malachi Toney caught 12 passes for a school-record 234 yards and three touchdowns to lead No. 7 Miami to a comfortable 45-6 victory at Stanford on Friday night. Mensah completed 27 of 30 passes for Miami (1-0, 1-0 Atlantic Coast Conference). He joined C.J. Stroud and Dillon Gabriel as the only quarterbacks since 2021 to complete 90% of their passes and throw for 400 or more yards and five or more touchdowns in a game. Toney broke the old school mark of 220 receiving yards set by Eddie Brown in a 1984 loss to Boston College that is remembered for a game-ending Hail Mary touchdown pass by Eagles quarterback Doug Flutie. The Cardinal (1-1, 0-1) were unable to follow up a season-opening win over Hawaii, giving up 549 total yards. Davis Warren completed 21 of 41 passes for 214 yards but was held without a touchdown. No. 10 Oklahoma 51, UTEP 0 John Mateer threw for 225 yards and three touchdowns, helping lead the Sooners to a win over the Miners in Norman, Okla. Mateer completed 11 of 17 passes, with his touchdown passes all covering 34 yards or more. Isaiah Sategna III returned a punt 88 yards for a score and gained 76 yards on four catches for Oklahoma (1-0), which outgained UTEP 401-198. Backup quarterback Raymond Moore III ran for a team-high 49 yards for the Miners (0-1), while starter EJ Colson Jr. threw for 52 yards and ran for 25. No. 14 USC 39, Fresno State 0 Jayden Maiava completed 23 of 25 passes for 349 yards and threw all three of his touchdown passes in the first half as the Trojans routed the Bulldogs in Los Angeles. The Trojans (2-0) scored 23 points in the second quarter to put the game away. Maiava connected with freshman Trent Mosley on 68- and 9-yard scores in the quarter. Mosley finished the game with 104 yards. USC's Kennedy Urlacher had two sacks, the first of which resulted in points. With Fresno State (0-1) backed up near its goal line, he bull-rushed his way through a blocker and shoved Bulldogs quarterback Jayden Mandal out of the back of the end zone for a safety to make it 16-0. --Field Level Media

item.title: Philippine VP Duterte posts bail after arrest order for alleged grave threats
item.description: Philippine Vice President Sara Duterte posted bail on Saturday after a trial court ordered her arrest on three counts of grave threats linked to comments she made about President Ferdinand Marcos Jr, the first lady and a former House speaker.
item.dc:creator: Nestor Corrales, Eloisa Lopez
item.content:encoded: Philippine Vice President Sara Duterte posted bail on Saturday after a trial court [USN:L6N44W0FQ TEXT:"ordered her arrest"] on three counts of grave threats linked to comments she made about President Ferdinand Marcos Jr, the first lady and a former House speaker. The arrest order marks an escalation in Duterte’s legal troubles as she also faces an impeachment trial in the Senate, a process that, if it ends in conviction, could remove her from office and derail her 2028 [USN:P8N3T403W TEXT:"presidential bid."] It is the latest step in a feud between the dominant Philippine political dynasties. Marcos and Duterte, both the children of longtime presidents, formed an alliance in 2022 that allowed them to sweep to power before they broke with each other in 2024. Dressed in black and surrounded by dozens of police officers, Duterte told reporters outside the court that she did not feel safe and accused authorities of harassment, saying the case involved the president, the first lady and Marcos' cousin, heightening her fears. "If I post bail, the harassment won’t stop. If I don’t post bail, I’ll be taken to the police. I have no trust in the police, I have no trust in the courts. I do not feel safe at all," Duterte said. She asked who would be held accountable “if I die tonight,” saying police would simply “wash their hands and call it an accident.” The police accorded the vice president with the respect she deserved, Interior Minister Jonvic Remulla said when asked to comment on Duterte’s remarks. “It's very unfortunate that all the pressure in her life is affecting her perception,” Remulla said in a phone message. Marcos' office did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Duterte's remarks about her safety. The office said on Friday it would respect any decision or order issued by the court. The court found probable cause to try Duterte on all three counts and set bail at 120,000 pesos ($1,900) per count. The case stems from a November 2024 online press conference in which Duterte said she had spoken with an assassin and instructed him to [USN:L4N3MU01O TEXT:"kill Marcos,"] his wife Liza Araneta Marcos and his cousin, then-Speaker Martin Romualdez, if she herself were killed. She has denied threatening them. The alleged threats are also part of the [USN:L6N4380IN TEXT:"impeachment complaint"] against her. Duterte also faces accusations of misusing public funds while vice president and during her tenure as education secretary, allegations she rejects. ($1 = 62.5960 Philippine pesos)

item.title: South Korea exports surpass full-year record, hit $709.4 billion YTD
item.description: South Korea's exports have reached $709.4 billion so far this year, surpassing last year's annual record, the customs office said on Saturday, as the economy rides high on booming global demand for AI chips.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South Korea's exports have reached $709.4 billion so far this year, surpassing last year's annual record, the customs office said on Saturday, as the economy rides high on booming global demand for AI chips. The country's exports hit $709.3 billion last year, a second consecutive annual record. Asia's fourth-largest economy is on track to reach $1 trillion in annual exports by early December, becoming the fourth country to hit the milestone after the United States, China and Germany, according to the Korea Customs Service. "Our exports continue to show remarkable growth momentum, even amid an uncertain trade environment due to strengthened protectionism, global supply chain restructuring and the Middle East situation," the customs office said. CHIPS ACCOUNT FOR 41% OF EXPORTS From January to August this year, semiconductor exports increased by 169.6% to $281 billion compared to the same period last year, representing 41% of total exports. South Korea is home to leading global memory chipmakers Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) and SK Hynix (000660.KS) , which are benefiting from surging prices as the AI investment boom exacerbates a chip shortage. Passenger cars, South Korea's No.2 export item, saw overseas shipments fall 4% during January to August from a year earlier. Korea's exports to China, its top export destination, jumped 76% during the period and shipments to the Untied States increased 57%, the data showed.

item.title: Jefferies-linked fund has almost $500 million exposure to trader Radiant World, FT reports
item.description: A fund run by a unit of U.S. bank Jefferies has nearly $500 million of exposure to iron ore trader Radiant World, its founder and another entity, the Financial Times reported on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A fund run by a unit of U.S. bank Jefferies (JEF.N) has nearly $500 million of exposure to iron ore trader Radiant World, its founder and another entity, the Financial Times reported on Saturday. [USN:L1N44V01X TEXT:"LAM Trade Finance Group II"], a fund run by a Jefferies unit and in which Jefferies holds a minority stake, secured a freezing order from a court in London against Radiant World, its founder Pinkesh Nahar and Sapphire Minmetals, which used to be part of Radiant World, Reuters reported on Wednesday, citing a person with knowledge of the matter. The FT said the freezing order was for up to $499 million, citing people familiar with the matter, putting the fund's exposure significantly higher than previously reported. Reuters has previously reported that Jefferies had trade-finance-related exposure of [USN:L1N43X0PT TEXT:"about $300 million"] to Radiant World through its Point Bonita fund. Point Bonita [USN:L3N3VP0ML TEXT:"drew attention last year"] after Jefferies disclosed it had hundreds of millions of dollars of exposure to bankrupt auto-parts maker First Brands Group. Jefferies and Radiant World did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment. Jefferies declined to comment to the FT. Radiant World has [USN:L1N44H0TU TEXT:"come under scrutiny"] due to concerns that invoices provided to its banks may not have been valid. The company has strongly denied the allegations, which have prompted some counterparties and lenders to halt or restrict business with it.

item.title: Pachuca gana como visitante a Bravos de Ciudad Juárez en torneo mexicano
item.description: Pachuca venció el viernes por 2-0 como visitante a Bravos de Ciudad Juárez en el inicio de la séptima jornada del torneo Apertura del fútbol mexicano donde debutó el argentino Gustavo Lema como director técnico del equipo derrotado.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Pachuca venció el viernes por 2-0 como visitante a Bravos de Ciudad Juárez en el inicio de la séptima jornada del torneo Apertura del fútbol mexicano donde debutó el argentino Gustavo Lema como director técnico del equipo derrotado. Lema fue nombrado técnico de Bravos el miércoles con el objetivo de sacar al equipo del último lugar del torneo, en donde el equipo no ha sumado puntos tras sufrir su séptima derrota. En el partido disputado en el estadio Olímpico Benito Juárez, Pachuca anotó el primer gol a los 53 minutos con un potente zurdazo del venezolano Salomón Rondón en el área chica tras controlar con el pecho un centro enviado por Carlos Sánchez desde el sector derecho. El segundo gol de los "Tuzos" de Pachuca cayó en tiempo de reposición cuando Alan Bautista definió ante la salida del portero tras eludir a tres adversarios después de recibir un pase del argentino Javier Vallejo a los 100 minutos. Con su segunda victoria, Pachuca llegó a 11 puntos para ubicarse momentáneamente en el undécimo lugar general. El sábado se jugarán los partidos entre Atlético de San Luis-Guadalajara, Tigres UANL-Necaxa y Atlas-Atlante El domingo, el vigente campeón Cruz Azul enfrentará a Santos Laguna. Los encuentros entre Pumas UNAM-León, Puebla-Toluca, América-Tijuana y Querétaro-Monterrey se pospusieron debido a la participación de América, Toluca, León y Monterrey en la Leagues Cup.

item.title: Africa's football progress seen as key factor in future support for Infantino
item.description: African football officials are prioritising development over governance disputes surrounding FIFA President Gianni Infantino and the continent's progress will guide future leadership decisions, said Benin Football Federation President Marcellin Bocove.
item.dc:creator: Iain Axon
item.content:encoded: African football officials are prioritising development over governance disputes surrounding FIFA President Gianni Infantino and the continent's progress will guide future leadership decisions, said Benin Football Federation President Marcellin Bocove. Bocove was speaking ahead of the FIFA under-20 Women's World Cup, which runs from Saturday through September 27 in Poland. The tournament is the first global FIFA competition since the [USN:L6N44V19H TEXT:"governance row"] triggered by Infantino's proposal to sell a [USN:L6N43U0Z6 TEXT:"stake in the World Cup"] to private investors. The Swiss administrator [USN:L1N43X04P TEXT:"abandoned the plan"], which valued the commercial rights of the World Cup and other FIFA tournaments at $20 billion, in late July in the face of a fierce backlash from European governing body UEFA and other stakeholders in the game. Infantino has apologised for "errors" made during the FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal, but subsequently defended the concept as a vehicle to distribute more money to poorer national soccer federations. Infantino, who has announced he will seek a fourth term in March 2027, has since faced calls to resign but retains support from the African and South American confederations. "It is not up to me to say whether he (Infantino) is the right person or not, but we look at the track record of what's been done over the past 10 years or so," Bocove told Reuters on the sidelines of Benin's training session in Katowice on Friday. "What is important for us is that Africa progresses in the development of football, and that is more what we will be basing our position on going forward." Asked whether Benin would vote for Infantino in the 2027 election, Bocove replied: "It's too early to answer such a question. We don't know how things will unfold by then ..." Bocove said recent years had brought tangible progress to African football but argued more investment was needed. "There is investment...," he added. "We need to continue, keep going in the same direction, and so that calls for even more investment, and so the needs are there, we have to address them." Similar views were expressed by Gideon Fosu, a member of the Ghana Football Association's executive committee. "I think genuinely the passion for Infantino to just want to help develop football in Africa, for me, is something that I admire," Fosu said. "I think that the support he requires is what I am hoping that everybody will look beyond setting boundaries ... "So if there's that structure there, that intention to develop the women's game and football as a whole in Africa, I think that is something that everybody should support." Four African teams are competing at the under-20 Women's World Cup: Benin, Nigeria, Ghana and Tanzania.

item.title: Blake Snell blanks Nats for 6 innings in Dodgers' win
item.description: Blake Snell delivered six scoreless innings, Kyle Tucker contributed a home run and the Los Angeles Dodgers earned a 5-3 victory over the visiting Washington Nationals on Friday in the opener of a three-game series.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Blake Snell delivered six scoreless innings, Kyle Tucker contributed a home run and the Los Angeles Dodgers earned a 5-3 victory over the visiting Washington Nationals on Friday in the opener of a three-game series. Teoscar Hernandez had a two-run double, one game after hitting a two-run game-ending double as the Dodgers won their second consecutive game without Shohei Ohtani, who is dealing with a sore knee, biceps and neck. Snell (3-1) gave up five hits with two walks and seven strikeouts and has allowed just three total runs in five starts since returning from a procedure to remove loose bodies from his elbow. James Wood had two doubles and drove in a run for the Nationals, who lost their second consecutive game after winning five of six. Jackson Kent (1-3) gave up four runs (three earned) on four hits with four walks and four strikeouts over five innings of his fifth career start. Washington dropped the opener of a six-game California road trip that also includes a stop at San Diego. Tucker started the Dodgers' three-run third with a walk and Enrique Hernandez followed with a free pass of his own. Mookie Betts had a one-out single for a 1-0 lead and Teoscar Hernandez followed with a two-run double to the exact spot in the outfield where he hit his game-ending double against the St. Louis Cardinals on Thursday. Los Angeles made it 4-0 in the fourth when Alex Call doubled against his former club and scored on a Tommy Edman ground ball that was misplayed by Nationals shortstop Nasim Nunez. In the final month of a disappointing season, Tucker came through with a home run in the sixth for a 5-0 Dodgers lead. It was just his 12th home run of the season, his third in 67 home games and his first since Aug. 8. The Nationals prevented a second consecutive shutout loss when Abimelec Ortiz had an RBI single in the ninth against Seth Halvorsen. Jorbit Vivas added an RBI groundout, and Wood doubled in a run to bring the tying run to the plate before Chaparro flied out to end the game. Jack Dreyer recorded the final three outs for his second save. --Field Level Media

item.title: LSU leaves former pro players off roster for opener vs. Clemson
item.description: The two former NFL players who returned to college to join the LSU program were not added to the Tigers' roster ahead of the Saturday season opener against visiting Clemson.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The two former NFL players who returned to college to join the LSU program were not added to the Tigers' roster ahead of the Saturday season opener against visiting Clemson. Tight end Dae'Quan Wright and defensive lineman Zxavian Harris will miss the Saturday contest but still could be added to the roster at a later date if they remain enrolled in school. LSU put only 103 players on the roster, and the limit is 105. Louisiana district court judge William Jorden issued a preliminary injunction on Thursday that cleared the way for Wright and Harris to play for the Tigers even though both were in NFL training camps this summer. Wright and Harris were 42 athletes across multiple sports who were covered by the injunction, which came in the wake of the NCAA's pivot to a new 5-for-5 eligibility system. The judge's ruling temporarily prevents the Southeastern Conference and the NCAA from enforcing rules that would keep the athletes from playing college sports in the new school year. Wright signed with the Philadelphia Eagles as an undrafted free agent in the offseason, then was claimed off waivers by the Cleveland Browns, who subsequently waived him last week. Harris signed an undrafted free agent contract with the New Orleans Saints before they waived him in early August. Both Harris and Wright played for new LSU coach Lane Kiffin last season at Ole Miss The SEC and the NCAA have vehemently opposed the return of athletes from the pro ranks to college programs, including a federal lawsuit filed by the SEC against Kiffin and a number of LSU administrators on Thursday in Alabama in an attempt to keep such players off college rosters. On Friday, Clemson's general counsel sent an email to LSU's general counsel, stating that using Harris or Wright may break "contractual obligations between the two parties" for the Saturday game, Yahoo Sports reported. The SEC passed a rule last week that permitted commissioner Greg Sankey to punish any school that added players who signed NFL contracts to its roster. A half-season suspension of the head coach and a fine of half of the school's football athletic budget were the prescribed penalties. The conference approved the measure regarding the penalties by a 15-0 count, with LSU abstaining. --Field Level Media

item.title: Luis Campusano's 2-run, 10th-inning blast carries Padres past Yankees
item.description: Luis Campusano belted a two-run homer in the bottom of the 10th inning Friday night, giving the San Diego Padres a 3-2 win over the visiting New York Yankees.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Luis Campusano belted a two-run homer in the bottom of the 10th inning Friday night, giving the San Diego Padres a 3-2 win over the visiting New York Yankees. With Dustin Harris at second, pinch-running for the automatic runner, Paul Blackburn (7-3) fanned Xander Bogaerts for the first out. Campusano then belted a first-pitch sinker an estimated 394 feet to the seats in left for his sixth homer of the year and his second walk-off hit of the season. Mason Miller (5-2) pitched two innings to earn the win despite allowing Spencer Jones' RBI single in the top of the 10th that gave New York a short-lived 2-1 edge. The result allowed San Diego (74-67) to take a half-game lead on the Arizona Diamondbacks (74-68) for the National League's last wild-card spot. San Diego won for just the second time in seven games. The Yankees (80-61) dropped four games behind the Tampa Bay Rays (84-57) in the American League East and saw their lead over the Boston Red Sox (77-65) for the AL's first wild-card spot fall to 3 1/2 games. Both starters ended up without a decision despite pitching well. New York's Max Fried yielded a run and four hits in 5 2/3 innings, walking one and whiffing four. San Diego's Walker Buehler permitted three hits and a run in five innings, issuing two walks and striking out six. San Diego took a 1-0 lead in the second inning. Ty France led off with the first of his two doubles and was sacrificed to third by Jackson Merrill. After Austin Hays popped up for the second out, Bogaerts looped a single to center that drove in France. Buehler's only mistake tied the game with two outs in the third. Ben Rice cracked his 36th homer of the year, launching a hanging slider an estimated 444 feet over the center field wall. The Padres could have earned their 10th walk-off win of the year in the ninth after France doubled with one out. However, Merrill's deep fly ball to left was chased down by Cody Bellinger, and after a passed ball moved the runner to third, David Bednar struck out Hays to force extra innings. --Field Level Media

item.title: Alcaraz tones down the tank top after revealing too much
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz's headline-grabbing U.S. Open tank top came with an extra layer of modesty on Friday after the Spaniard said that he had revealed "too much nipple" during his first two matches.
item.dc:creator: Janina Rios
item.content:encoded: Carlos Alcaraz's headline-grabbing U.S. Open tank top came with an extra layer of modesty on Friday after the Spaniard said that he had revealed "too much nipple" during his first two matches. In a tournament where outfits have drawn attention in both the men's and women's draws, Alcaraz's loose-fitting brown Nike tank top, a Travis Scott x Cactus Jack collaboration, kept slipping to expose his chest. The seven-times Grand Slam champion's outfit prompted plenty of memes and witty comments online, with former WTA Tour player Eugenie Bouchard jokingly telling him to "put the nip away." For his third-round match with China's Wu Yibing on Friday, Alcaraz stepped onto Arthur Ashe Stadium wearing a white undershirt beneath his kit. "I think I've been seeing too much of my nipples lately," Alcaraz told reporters with a laugh after his [USN:L4N44W186 TEXT:"6-3 6-4 6-1 win"]. The 23-year-old confirmed that the decision to add the undershirt was entirely his own. "I feel really comfortable with another shirt. So I think I'm going to stay like that," he added. Alcaraz, who is returning from more than four months out with a wrist injury, has lost one set through his first three singles matches at Flushing Meadows. He next faces American 20th seed Tommy Paul, an opponent he has beaten five times in a row. "He's a really talented player, really difficult one to play," Alcaraz said. "I think he's really dangerous for everyone on the tour. I'm really looking forward to playing him once again."

item.title: One dead, 11 people missing after mudslide in China's Jiangxi province
item.description: One person has been confirmed dead and 11 others remain missing after torrential rains triggered a mudslide early Saturday morning in a town in China's Jiangxi Province, local authorities said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: One person has been confirmed dead and 11 others remain missing after torrential rains triggered a mudslide early Saturday morning in a town in China's Jiangxi Province, local authorities said. Due to heavy rainfall brought by Typhoon Saudel, the mudslide struck around 4 a.m. (2000 GMT Friday) Saturday in Gaoping Town of Jiangxi's Suichuan County, damaging 12 houses, the county said in a statement. State broadcaster CCTV also reported more than 10 people were trapped after the landslide hit the same town, state broadcasters CCTV reported.

item.title: Ivan Herrera's 9th-inning homer rescues Cardinals against Rockies
item.description: Ivan Herrera hit a three-run homer in the ninth inning, and the St. Louis Cardinals rallied to beat the Colorado Rockies 7-6 in Denver on Friday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Ivan Herrera hit a three-run homer in the ninth inning, and the St. Louis Cardinals rallied to beat the Colorado Rockies 7-6 in Denver on Friday night. St. Louis (71-71) gained ground in the NL wild-card race, pulling even with Miami and moving within three games of Arizona. The Cardinals trailed 6-4 entering the ninth when Thomas Saggese drew a leadoff walk from Jordan Romano (0-3) and stole second before Jose Fermin reached on a throwing error. Herrera hit a 1-2 slider 430 feet to center to give St. Louis the lead with manager Oliver Marmol watching from the clubhouse. Marmol was ejected in the sixth inning by home plate umpire Doug Eddings. Cade Winquest (1-0) got his first major league win with 1 2/3 innings of scoreless relief. Riley O'Brien recorded the final three outs for his 36th save. Cole Carrigg hit an inside-the-park home run and tripled, TJ Rumfield also went deep, tripled and singled, and Connor Norby had two hits for Colorado (54-87). St. Louis starter Andre Pallante battled through five innings, allowing just a run, and left with a 4-1 lead, and the Rockies pounced on reliever Hancel Rincon, who was making his major league debut. With one out, Rumfield tripled and scored on a wild pitch, Carrigg's drive bounced off the wall in center, and he scored easily. It was his seventh home run. Norby singled and Justin Bruihl relieved Rincon. He was given a pitch clock violation before throwing a pitch, bringing out Marmol, who was ejected. Johnston doubled, Adael Amador had an RBI single and Johnston scored on Zac Veen's sacrifice bunt. Replays showed catcher Leo Bernal tagged out Johnston, but St. Louis lost its challenge. Rumfield hit a solo homer in the seventh, his 15th, to extend the lead. The Rockies took a 1-0 lead on Hunter Goodman's sacrifice fly in the first, but St. Louis answered in the second on Nolan Gorman's run-scoring single and an RBI double by Saggese. The Cardinals padded their lead in the fifth on Alec Burleson's RBI single and Walker's sacrifice fly. Feltner allowed four runs on seven hits in five innings. --Field Level Media

item.title: Jonathan Aranda's big night helps Rays beat Rangers
item.description: Jonathan Aranda doubled, homered, drove in two runs and scored two for the Tampa Bay Rays in a 7-6 win against the Texas Rangers on Friday night in the second game of their four-game series in Arlington, Texas.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jonathan Aranda doubled, homered, drove in two runs and scored two for the Tampa Bay Rays in a 7-6 win against the Texas Rangers on Friday night in the second game of their four-game series in Arlington, Texas. Richie Palacios homered, Yandy Diaz had three hits and scored a run and Junior Caminero had two hits and two RBIs for the Rays (84-57), who had lost two in a row. Tampa Bay right-hander Nick Martinez (14-4) allowed three runs and five hits in 6 1/3 innings. He struck out four and walked two. Elias Diaz hit a grand slam in the seventh that made it a one-run game, and Ezequiel Duran also homered for the Rangers (70-72), who had won four of five. Texas started with right-hander Trevor Williams. He threw a scoreless first inning before handing off to left-hander Robby Ahlstrom, who stranded the bases loaded in the second. Kumar Rocker (5-11) then came in to handle the bulk of the innings and he was tagged for six runs (five earned) and nine hits in five innings. He struck out three and didn't walk a batter. Duran led off the second with a home run and Aranda matched him in the third to tie it 1-1. Palacios homered with two outs in the fourth for a 2-1 lead. Diaz, Aranda and Caminero started the fifth with three straight doubles for a 4-1 lead. After getting the first out of the inning, Rocker gave up a blooper to shallow center by Victor Mesa Jr., who took second on an error by Evan Carter in center while Caminero was scoring for a 5-1 lead. The Rays tacked on one more run in the inning when Mesa scored during a rundown to make it 6-1. Diaz lined a two-strike slider over the fence in left for a grand slam that cut it to 6-5. Caminero gave the Rays some insurance with an RBI single in the ninth that made it 7-5. Bryan Baker started the ninth for Tampa Bay before departing with a trainer after walking the first two batters. He told reporters after the game that he left due to dehydration. Tyler Wells entered and the runners advanced on a sacrifice bunt. Diaz hit a sacrifice fly to cut it to 7-6 before Wells got the final out. --Field Level Media

item.title: Sydney sweats in spring hot spell, faces 'extreme' bushfire risk
item.description: Australia's most populous city Sydney baked in a burst of sweltering spring heat on Saturday, raising the risk of bushfires and prompting authorities to issue a ban on lighting fires.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Australia's most populous city Sydney baked in a burst of sweltering spring heat on Saturday, raising the risk of bushfires and prompting authorities to issue a ban on lighting fires. The heat comes as a powerful El Nino [USN:P8N40Z06Q TEXT:"weather pattern"] in the Pacific, expected to be among the strongest in decades, drives hotter and drier conditions across southern Australia during the September-November spring season. On Saturday, the nation's weather forecaster said temperatures in the New South Wales capital, home to 5.6 million people, were set to hit 33 degrees Celsius (91.4 degrees Fahrenheit), nearly 13C above average. At Sydney Airport, the temperature was already 28.6C (83.48F) at 11:30 a.m. (0130 GMT)local time, more than seven degrees above the September mean maximum temperature, according to forecaster data. "Fresh to strong and gusty northwesterly winds developing during the morning, combined with dry, unseasonably warm conditions, will result in elevated fire dangers across the Greater Sydney Region today," the forecaster said. State fire authorities issued a total fire ban for Sydney where they rated fire risk as "extreme", the second highest danger rating. Climate change is causing extreme heat and fire weather to become more common in Australia, a bushfire-prone country of around 27 million. In January, thousands of firefighters [USN:L4N3YA1ME TEXT:"battled bushfires"] in the southeast that razed homes, cut power to thousands of homes and burned swathes of bushland.

item.title: Williams sisters' US Open return becomes celebration despite first-round exit
item.description: Four years after what seemed like their final bow, Serena and Venus Williams transformed a first-round U.S. Open doubles defeat into a celebration of tennis in front of 23,000 adoring fans at Arthur Ashe Stadium on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Janina Rios
item.content:encoded: Four years after what seemed like their final bow, Serena and Venus Williams transformed a first-round U.S. Open doubles defeat into a celebration of tennis in front of 23,000 adoring fans at Arthur Ashe Stadium on Friday. Australia's Maya Joint and Taiwan's Chan Hao-ching emerged with a 6-3 6-7(6) 7-6(10-7) win, but for much of the contest the score felt irrelevant as fans roared at every Williams winner and fell into virtual silence at every point in between. Serena, 44, walked onto court wearing a shiny customized bomber jacket decorated with patches marking her U.S. Open singles and doubles triumphs. Her 46-year-old sister stodd alongside, the pair carrying matching pink bags. The comeback, which Serena said was at the suggestion of her daughter, carried the weight of more than two decades: 14 Grand Slam doubles titles together, two U.S. Open crowns, three Olympic gold medals, and another 30 Grand Slam singles titles between them. Joint and Chan, the 14th seeds, weathered the hostile atmosphere to take the opening set, but the Williams sisters hit back in the second, riding the crowd's energy to force a third set. The Americans showed they had lost none of their grit, going toe-to-toe with the younger pair, spurred on by a raucous crowd desperate to carry their long-time idols over the finish line. But Joint and Chan edged the super tiebreak in dramatic fashion, sealing victory in just over three hours. "Being able to play against such legends of the game is super special," said Joint on court. The reunion had been a long time coming. The sisters were forced to withdraw from the Wimbledon doubles draw after Serena suffered a knee injury in singles, leaving New York as the stage for the comeback fans had been waiting for. Joint, 20, beat Serena at Wimbledon in the only singles match of her comeback and the Australian struggled to sum up the Flushing Meadows experience. "I'm lost for words to think of it," she said. "She's my idol, both of them. I grew up in Michigan so I always looked up to them. Being able to play them twice is amazing." The Williams sisters had arrived in Flushing Meadows with little recent doubles form together, having lost in three sets to Marta Kostyuk and Peyton Stearns in Cincinnati. Serena had already given New York a taste of the magic, though, teaming up with Carlos Alcaraz for a mixed doubles run that ended in the quarter-finals. Whether the sisters team up again is uncertain, so for the crowd at Flushing Meadows on Friday, seeing Serena's clenched fist and Venus at her side made it a night to remember.

item.title: Yankees OF Trent Grisham injures hamstring in loss to Padres
item.description: New York Yankees center fielder Trent Grisham is likely headed for an MRI exam and could land on the injured list after exiting Friday night's game against the host San Diego Padres with a right hamstring injury.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: New York Yankees center fielder Trent Grisham is likely headed for an MRI exam and could land on the injured list after exiting Friday night's game against the host San Diego Padres with a right hamstring injury. Grisham was visibly limping while running in on Xander Bogaerts' two-out fly ball into shallow left-center that fell for a single to score Ty France in the bottom of the second. Before the Yankees took the field in the third, Grisham was replaced by Heliot Ramos in the lineup with Spencer Jones switching from right to center field. After the game -- a 3-2 Padres win in 10 innings -- Yankees manager Aaron Boone said Grisham aggravated the injury trying to steal second base in the top of the second. "I'm not sure yet if it's an IL or not, but it certainly could be," Boone said. Grisham spent time on the IL in June because of a strained right hamstring. Grisham is batting .211 with 18 homers and 59 RBIs in 121 games this season. --Field Level Media

item.title: Yainer Diaz's homer helps rising Astros down Diamondbacks
item.description: Yainer Diaz homered, Cristian Javier matched his season high in strikeouts and the Houston Astros claimed the opener of their three-game interleague series against the visiting Arizona Diamondbacks with a 3-1 victory on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Yainer Diaz homered, Cristian Javier matched his season high in strikeouts and the Houston Astros claimed the opener of their three-game interleague series against the visiting Arizona Diamondbacks with a 3-1 victory on Friday. Javier (2-5) allowed one run on one hit with three walks and eight strikeouts in five innings. Josh Hader struck out the side in the ninth inning for his 23rd save of the season, making him the 41st player in history to record 250 career saves. The Astros (73-69) reached a season-high four games over .500 this season by winning for the seventh time in their past nine games. Houston improved to 4-1 on its seven-game homestand. Arizona (74-68) took its fourth loss in five games. Diaz keyed the Astros' three-run third inning with a leadoff blast to left field off Merrill Kelly (9-13). The Houston catcher lined a 1-0 slider 383 feet for his 11th home run of the season and a 1-0 lead. Kelly responded by striking out LaMonte Wade Jr., but Jeremy Pena and Yordan Alvarez followed with singles. Isaac Paredes hit an RBI double, and Jose Altuve plated Alvarez with a sacrifice fly to left field, extending the Astros' advantage to 3-0. The third inning represented the lone hiccup for Kelly. He surrendered just two more hits, both singles, and did not allow another baserunner to reach scoring position. Kelly worked six innings, allowing three runs on seven hits and no walks while striking out four. Javier fanned a pair of batters in the top of the first and sidestepped a leadoff walk to Ketel Marte in the second. He struck out Corbin Carroll for a second time to strand Geraldo Perdomo at second in the third and added two strikeouts in both the fourth and fifth innings. Gabriel Moreno smacked his 12th home run leading off the fourth, a 387-foot drive to left-center, to mar Javier's line. Astros relievers Enyel De Los Santos, Bennett Sousa, Bryan Abreu and Hader preserved the lead. Abreu benefited from a nifty double play started by Pena in the eighth. The shortstop fielded a Marte grounder and tagged Moreno before he could scurry back to second. Pena had enough time to fire to first before Marte arrived. --Field Level Media

item.title: Seattle Times, Newsday sue OpenAI, Microsoft, alleging copyright infringement
item.description: The Seattle Times and Newsday sued OpenAI and Microsoft on Friday, alleging in federal court that the tech companies copied the newspapers' journalism without permission to train their AI systems.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Seattle Times and Newsday sued OpenAI and Microsoft (MSFT.O) on Friday, alleging in federal court that the tech companies copied the newspapers' journalism without permission to train their AI systems. The suit in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York alleges that OpenAI and Microsoft scraped the newspapers' websites, including content behind paywalls, and incorporated articles into datasets used to train and operate products including ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot and Bing's AI features. The newspapers, based in Seattle and Long Island, New York, said the companies' AI products can reproduce passages from their reporting, closely paraphrase articles and provide users with answers that reduce the need to visit their websites or buy subscriptions. "We feel strongly that we must defend our content - which we spend millions of dollars a year to produce - from being used without our consent or compensation," Seattle Times President and CEO Alan Fisco wrote to employees, according to the newspaper. A spokesperson for San Francisco-based OpenAI said its models are trained on publicly available data and grounded in fair use, without commenting specifically on the lawsuit. A spokesperson for Microsoft, based near Seattle in Washington state, said in an email: "While we’re surprised by the lawsuit, we appreciate the importance of local journalism and we’re always happy to sit down and explore solutions to this type of dispute." The Seattle Times and Newsday are seeking an order requiring the destruction of copies of their works as well as training datasets or AI models incorporating them. The lawsuit echoes a case filed by [USN:L6N44U18K TEXT:"the New York Times"] (NYT.N) in 2023, which accused OpenAI and Microsoft (MSFT.O) of using millions of newspaper articles without permission to train OpenAI's popular chatbot. The case is ongoing, and is one of dozens brought by copyright holders against tech companies such as OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta for what they say is misuse of their material to train AI systems. (This story has been refiled to say 'a,' not 'an' spokesperson, in the fourth bullet point.)

item.title: Alejandro Kirk, Ernie Clement spark Blue Jays past Royals
item.description: Alejandro Kirk and Ernie Clement had two hits and a pair of RBIs apiece to help the visiting Toronto Blue Jays post a 9-2 victory over the Kansas City Royals on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Alejandro Kirk and Ernie Clement had two hits and a pair of RBIs apiece to help the visiting Toronto Blue Jays post a 9-2 victory over the Kansas City Royals on Friday. After Toronto starter Jameson Taillon exited with elbow discomfort following two innings, four relievers combined to throw seven innings of one-run ball. Michael Lorenzen earned a rare three-inning save to close the door. George Springer also drove in two runs for the Blue Jays (71-71), who won their sixth game in seven tries, pulling within a game of the Cleveland Guardians for the final American League wild-card slot. Daniel Lynch IV (4-5) allowed five runs on seven hits across five innings while walking one for the Royals (63-79), who have lost four of their last five. Bobby Witt Jr. and Vinnie Pasquantino bookended the loss with solo homers for Kansas City. Toronto jumped on Lynch early, as Brett Bateman was hit by a pitch and Vladimir Guerrero Jr. slashed a one-out single in the top of the first. Kirk and Kazuma Okamoto then lined consecutive RBI base hits to give the visitors a 2-0 edge. Two batters later, Clement hit his 30th double of the season to extend the first-inning margin to four. Witt helped cut into the deficit in the bottom of the first, as he connected on his 17th homer of the year -- a 410-foot solo shot. Myles Straw and Guerrero singled in the second, before Kirk drove in another run with a double to center. Taillon was relieved after the second inning by Joe Mantiply (2-0), who tossed two scoreless frames. Nolan Hoffman entered for Lynch in the sixth. The Kansas City reliever was greeted with singles from Clement and Nathan Lukes and Straw's run-scoring sacrifice bunt. Brett Bateman then walked and Springer followed with a two-run double to make it 8-1. Rookie first baseman Sean Keys entered as a defensive replacement for Guerrero in the eighth. Keys led off the top of the ninth with his second career homer off Kansas City reliever Easton McGee. --Field Level Media

item.title: Bolivie-Explosion dans une caserne, deux morts et des disparus
item.description: Au moins deux personnes ont été tuées et des dizaines d'autres blessées vendredi lors d'une explosion dans une caserne militaire de la ville de Viacha, à une trentaine de kilomètres de la capitale bolivienne La Paz, a déclaré le ministre de la Défense, Ernesto Justiniano.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Au moins deux personnes ont été tuées et des dizaines d'autres blessées vendredi lors d'une explosion dans une caserne militaire de la ville de Viacha, à une trentaine de kilomètres de la capitale bolivienne La Paz, a déclaré le ministre de la Défense, Ernesto Justiniano. Selon un communiqué de son ministère, 14 personnes sont portées disparues. L'explosion est survenue vers 14h30 (18h30 GMT) dans une zone utilisée pour stocker du matériel pyrotechnique, ont fait savoir les autorités. La cause de l'explosion doit encore être établie. Des responsables ont toutefois déclaré qu'elle s'était produite dans la réserve de feux d'artifice du ministère de la Défense. La directrice des services de santé de Viacha, Rita Nebraska, a dit à la télévision locale qu'il était estimé qu'entre dix et 15 personnes avait péri dans l'incident, et que 62 autres étaient blessées. La police a déclaré que plus de 50 personnes avaient été blessées et que des dizaines d'habitations avaient subi des dégâts. Rita Nebraska a dit que les pompiers avaient prévenus qu'une autre explosion était possible en raison de la chaleur sur place et qu'ils avaient appelé les habitants à se tenir à au moins 150 mètres du site.

item.title: Fifth-inning uprising rallies Brewers past Reds
item.description: Rookie Cooper Pratt ripped a bases-clearing triple and scored on a wild pitch during the fifth inning, lifting the visiting Milwaukee Brewers to a 10-7 victory over the Cincinnati Reds on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Rookie Cooper Pratt ripped a bases-clearing triple and scored on a wild pitch during the fifth inning, lifting the visiting Milwaukee Brewers to a 10-7 victory over the Cincinnati Reds on Friday. Milwaukee's Brice Turang had a two-run double among his three hits, drove in a run after being hit by a pitch with the bases loaded and also scored on a groundout. David Hamilton had an RBI triple and William Contreras added a run-scoring double for the Brewers (88-54), who own the majors' best record and have won seven of their last 10 games. Cincinnati's Eugenio Suarez belted a three-run homer in his return from a two-game absence in order to take the U.S. naturalization test. With his new walk-up song being Lee Greenwood's "God Bless The USA," the Venezuela-born Suarez deposited a 2-2 fastball from Shane Drohan over the wall in center field. The homer, which staked Cincinnati (67-74) to a 6-4 lead in the third, was the 21st of the season for Suarez and his third in six games. Milwaukee responded with a flourish by loading the bases against Rhett Lowder (6-9), who was relieved by Sam Moll. Turang was hit by a pitch, and Pratt followed with a bases-clearing triple down the right field line before scoring on a wild pitch to give the Brewers a 9-6 lead. Chad Patrick (8-4) relieved Drohan and allowed one hit over two scoreless innings. Drohan gave up six runs on five hits over four innings. Rookie Sal Stewart had an RBI single in the seventh to cut Milwaukee's lead to 10-7. Aaron Ashby fanned two in the eighth for the Brewers and Trevor Megill struck out the side in the ninth to secure his 26th save of the season. Lowder permitted seven runs (six earned) on six hits in four innings. Elly De La Cruz's RBI single to left field opened the scoring in the first before Milwaukee scratched for a pair of runs in the second, highlighted by Hamilton's RBI triple down the right field line. Matt McLain sent a 1-2 fastball from Drohan over the wall in left-center to give Cincinnati a 3-2 lead in the second. However, Turang's two-run double regained the lead for the Brewers in the third. --Field Level Media

item.title: Nolan McLean wins 3rd straight as Mets down Giants
item.description: Nolan McLean worked through six innings and won his third straight decision Friday night, when the host New York Mets beat the San Francisco Giants 10-6 in the opener of a three-game series.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Nolan McLean worked through six innings and won his third straight decision Friday night, when the host New York Mets beat the San Francisco Giants 10-6 in the opener of a three-game series. Mark Vientos hit a three-run homer in the first to give the Mets (64-77) a lead they'd never relinquish. Francisco Alvarez went deep twice while Bo Bichette and Francisco Lindor each had two-run homers. Juan Soto hit into an RBI forceout for the Mets, who have won four of six. Lindor, Vientos, Alvarez and Bichette all finished with two hits apiece. Rafael Devers was 3-for-4 with five RBIs via a two-RBI double and a three-run homer, for the Giants (58-84), who have dropped three of four. Turner Hill finished 2-for-4 with a run-scoring single in the sixth. Jonah Cox had two hits and scored two runs after entering as a pinch-hitter in the seventh. McLean (11-8) allowed two runs on six hits and four walks while striking out seven. The rookie right-hander had just two 1-2-3 innings but limited the Giants to two hits in 11 plate appearances with runners in scoring position. He wriggled out of a bases-loaded, none-out jam in the fifth when McLean struck out Jung Hoo Lee before getting Drew Cavanaugh to hit into a double play. McLean is 3-0 with a 1.08 ERA in his last four starts. Jefry Yan and Austin Warren combined to give up four runs in 1 2/3 innings. Warren surrendered Devers' blast with two outs in the eighth before Robert Stock, who made his first six appearances this season as a starter, recorded the final out. Alvarez's second homer in the bottom of the inning removed the save situation for Kodai Senga, who threw a hitless ninth. Rookie Matt Wilkinson (0-3) took the loss for the Giants after giving up seven runs (four earned) on five hits and two walks while striking out two over three innings. Yunior Marte went the rest of the way and allowed three runs on four hits and two walks while striking out two. --Field Level Media

item.title: Shota Imanaga leads Cubs past Marlins into top wild-card spot
item.description: Shota Imanaga outdueled Janson Junk on Friday to lead the Chicago Cubs to a 6-1 win over the host Miami Marlins.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Shota Imanaga outdueled Janson Junk on Friday to lead the Chicago Cubs to a 6-1 win over the host Miami Marlins. The Cubs won their second straight game and took over the top spot in the National League wild-card standings, thanks to their starter. The Cubs' left-hander dominated the Marlins, pitching into the seventh inning for the first time since July 31. Imanaga (9-10) allowed one run on three hits and no walks over six-plus innings. He departed after Griffin Conine led off the seventh with a hard-hit single. Conine (2-for-4) scored on an Esteury Ruiz groundout in the seventh. Cubs batters took advantage of Marlins relievers' wildness, scoring three runs in the sixth and another in the seventh. Jack Ralston walked three of the four batters he faced, and Josh Ekness followed by allowing another walk and two hits, as the Cubs broke open a one-run game. Only 12 of their 34 pitches were strikes in the decisive sixth. Prior to that, Junk (6-9) nearly matched Imanaga over five innings. He allowed three hits and a walk, with the only run coming on a Pedro Ramirez fielder's choice in the second inning. Junk retired 11 of the last 12 batters he faced. Nico Hoerner went 3-for-4 with an RBI. Alex Bregman extended his hitting streak to eight games thanks to a 2-for-4 night with a walk and a run scored and Michael Busch (1-for-4) added a ninth-inning solo home run, his 18th of the season. Pete Crow-Armstrong (1-for-4, two runs and a stolen base) started the seventh with a double and eventually scored on a Bradley Blalock wild pitch. The Cubs center fielder also made a highlight-reel catch, leaping at the left-center field wall to rob Heriberto Hernandez of an extra-base hit in the sixth. Aaron Civale, who relieved Imanaga in the seventh, suffered from some wildness as well. He allowed two two-out walks to load the bases in the inning but got pinch hitter Joe Mack looking at a curveball that dropped into the strike zone to end the threat. Civale then retired the last six batters in order to earn his second save of the season. --Field Level Media

item.title: US embassy issues health alert for Cuba amid oil blockade, sanctions
item.description: The U.S. embassy in Havana issued a health alert for Cuba on Friday, warning travelers and residents of a spike in intestinal illnesses and diarrhea caused by failing water and electricity supply, even as the Trump administration continued to hold back fuel shipments necessary for power generation on the island.
item.dc:creator: Dave Sherwood
item.content:encoded: The U.S. embassy in Havana issued a health alert for Cuba on Friday, warning travelers and residents of a spike in intestinal illnesses and diarrhea caused by failing water and electricity supply, even as the Trump administration continued to hold back fuel shipments necessary for power generation on the island. "The U.S. Embassy has noted a significant increase in diarrheal illness across Cuba, associated with the continuing degradation of the water and energy infrastructure," the alert stated. "This degradation affects water supply, and food storage and temperature control." The U.S. warning comes nine months after the Trump administration imposed a fuel blockade on the communist-run island, contributing to a sharp spike in power cuts and complicating refrigeration and sanitary measures in homes and businesses. U.N.-appointed human rights experts have called the Trump fuel blockade a violation of international law. A team of [USN:S8N41J077 TEXT:"U.N. experts"] in August warned of a growing risk of disease outbreaks on the island as the U.S. has tightened sanctions. "The humanitarian consequences are already unfolding into a full-blown crisis, threatening the rights to health, to life, to food and to development," the experts said. The Trump administration says sanctions are necessary to force a change in the island's government, a decades-long aim of the U.S. following Fidel Castro's 1959 revolution. Trump has called Cuba a national security threat to the United States. Residents throughout Cuba have for months complained of rampant illnesses that cause several days of diarrhea, fever and body aches, leaving many bedridden. During the Caribbean's sultry summer, sleep without air conditioning or a fan often becomes impossible, as does food preservation without refrigeration. Blackouts spanning days have become commonplace amid the U.S. fuel blockade. The U.S. health alert on Friday advised travelers and residents in Cuba to "be cautious of ... perishable foods that may have been inadequately stored," and warned against eating "foods that appear to have been sitting at room temperature for extended periods."

item.title: White Sox ride trio of homers to victory over Twins
item.description: Colson Montgomery went 1-for-4 with a two-run home run, and the Chicago White Sox pulled away for a 4-1 win over the visiting Minnesota Twins on Friday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Colson Montgomery went 1-for-4 with a two-run home run, and the Chicago White Sox pulled away for a 4-1 win over the visiting Minnesota Twins on Friday night. Miguel Vargas and Braden Montgomery each hit solo homers for Chicago (74-67) in the opener of a three-game series. The AL Central-leading White Sox ended a two-game skid. Josh Bell went 2-for-3 and homered to mark the lone run for Minnesota (67-74). Kody Clemens finished 3-for-4 for the Twins, who have dropped back-to-back games after winning three in a row. White Sox right-hander Erick Fedde (8-8) defeated the Twins for the second time in less than a week. He held Minnesota to three hits in five scoreless innings, walked two and struck out two. Twins right-hander Zebby Matthews (9-9) surrendered all four runs on four hits in five innings. He walked one and struck out four. The defeat marked the first time in six starts that Matthews did not earn a victory. The White Sox struck quickly in the bottom of the first inning. Matthews fired a fastball low and away, and Vargas took it the opposite direction for a homer to right-center field. The blast marked Vargas' 30th home run of the season. His previous high was 16, which he set with the White Sox in 2025. Braden Montgomery made it 2-0 with a blast in the second. He ripped a line-drive home run 419 feet to right-center field. The power surge continued in the fourth as the White Sox increased their lead to 4-0. After Andrew Benintendi drew a one-out walk, Colson Montgomery hammered a towering, 416-foot homer into the right-center-field bleachers for his 30th of the season. His previous career high was 21, set last year as a rookie. Bell put the Twins on the scoreboard in the ninth. He took right-hander Grant Taylor deep to right-center field for his 18th homer of the season. Bell's homer and a double by Royce Lewis marked the Twins' only extra-base hits. --Field Level Media

item.title: Chris Mueller, who once recorded brace for USMNT, retires
item.description: Marking the end of an eventful career, Chicago Fire FC winger Chris Mueller announced his retirement from professional soccer on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Marking the end of an eventful career, Chicago Fire FC winger Chris Mueller announced his retirement from professional soccer on Friday. Mueller made an impression in two caps for the U.S. Men's National Team. He recorded a brace in the USMNT's 6-0 win over El Salvador in a friendly in 2020. Mueller was diagnosed with pericarditis in 2025, which cost him the season. He returned for the Fire in February, making his debut in a preseason friendly against the LA Galaxy. He appeared in five regular-season games with one start. "Goodbyes are never easy, especially when you're waving farewell to a game you've centered the last 20 years of your life around," Mueller said in a statement provided to the Fire. "With that being said, this has been a decision that hasn't come without real challenge, a hefty amount of consideration, and serious contemplation." Mueller, 30, is a native of Illinois and joined the Fire in 2022, fulfilling a lifelong dream of suiting up for his childhood club. In 66 appearances over the next five seasons, Mueller tallied six goals and 10 assists. "Thank you to the Chicago Fire, firstly, for bringing me home and allowing me to play for my childhood club," Mueller said. "And secondly, but more importantly, for their support throughout me battling through this diagnosis. Truly, it was unbelievable and I never felt alone in it. "I'm beyond excited to see where the Club continues to head and for the victories that are yet to come. Thank you, Chicago. A supporter, I will always be." Prior to joining Chicago, Mueller had stints with Orlando City (2018-21) and Hibernian F.C. of the Scottish Premiership (2022). His four-year run with Orlando resulted in 21 goals and 24 assists in 112 appearances. --Field Level Media

item.title: Jared Jones fans 9 as Pirates blank Angels
item.description: Jared Jones matched his season high with nine strikeouts over six three-hit innings and Jake Mangum had an RBI double to lead the Pittsburgh Pirates to a 1-0 victory over the visiting Los Angeles Angels in the opener of a three-game series on Friday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jared Jones matched his season high with nine strikeouts over six three-hit innings and Jake Mangum had an RBI double to lead the Pittsburgh Pirates to a 1-0 victory over the visiting Los Angeles Angels in the opener of a three-game series on Friday night. Bryan Reynolds also doubled and had two hits for Pittsburgh (70-72), which won for the fifth time in its last six games. Konnor Griffin, activated off the 60-day injured list after missing 49 games with a torn sagittal band in his left ring finger, scored the lone run of the contest. Jones (3-6) walked one while snapping a seven-start winless drought dating back to a 7-1 victory at Cleveland on July 18. He left after throwing a season-high 91 pitches, 63 for strikes. Wilber Dotel followed Jones, recording two strikeouts and a walk over two innings, setting the stage for Mason Montgomery, who pitched around a leadoff single by Mike Trout in the ninth to pick up his ninth save. Ryan Johnson (3-8) suffered the loss for Los Angeles (53-88) despite allowing just one run on four hits in six innings. He walked two and struck out six. Pittsburgh scored the game's only run in the bottom of the second. Oneil Cruz led off with a walk but was erased at second on a fielder's choice by Griffin.
